**Claim:** `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`.

Branch: `claude/issue-6678-datasource-input-declaration-injection`.

Dispatched as ruled work, executing **option B in the injection form** per the 2026-08-29 director ruling — verbatim 「同意」. The injection form is the load-bearing part and travels into the order as such: the declaration is emitted **at the `ElementDataSourceGate` wrapping seam**, from the same place that reads the key, so the nine object-bound blocks get it from one mechanism rather than nine hand-kept copies that can drift.

⛔ Option A (adding `dataSource` to `BASE_PROPS`) is refused by the ruling and is out of scope: that set mirrors `BaseSchema`, and silencing the key on blocks that do not read it (`flex`, `card`) would make the diagnostic lie in the other direction. `packages/sdui-parser/src/validate.ts` is therefore **read-only** for this card.

Declared file face for the cross-lane in-flight check: `packages/react/src/` — `ElementDataSourceGate` and the wrapping seam where the injection lands — plus new pins. The nine wrapping registrations (`plugin-list`, `plugin-form`, `plugin-calendar`, `plugin-detail`, `plugin-charts`, `plugin-gantt`, `plugin-kanban`, `plugin-map`, `plugin-dashboard`) are expected to be read, and ⛔ NOT to receive nine hand-written copies of the declaration — if the injection cannot reach them from one place, that is a stop-and-report, not a licence to fan out.

The ruling's pins are the acceptance criterion, both directions: `dataSource` on a gate-wrapped block ⇒ no diagnostic and the binding works; `dataSource` on a **non-wrapped** block ⇒ `unknown-prop` still fires.

## Routing the implementer's cross-repo question — **option A**, and it travels as a card in the other repo's lane, not as a note here

The implementer corrected **objectui's** two parity gates rather than exempting them, and its ground for doing so is a measurement, not a preference: `PageComponentSchema.safeParse({ type, dataSource })` **succeeds and keeps the key** ⇒ `dataSource` is a **node-level** spec key, a sibling of `type` and `className`, while `ComponentPropsMap[type]` is only the per-block **PROPS** half of a node's contract. ⇒ the gate's complaint was measurably false, so exempting it would have left a false gate standing.

The same reasoning applies to the framework-side gate (`check:react-blocks-declaration-parity`, in **objectstack**), which reads the same two declarations and will raise the same false complaint once it next sees objectui's manifest. That one cannot be corrected from this repo.

**I agree with option A** and adopt the implementer's reasoning:

- **B (per-block exemptions upstream)** leaves a false gate standing behind an allowlist that needs a new entry every time a block starts wrapping the seam — *the drift the ruling refused, in another costume*. That phrase is exact: the whole point of the injection form was that no list is hand-kept.
- **C (move `dataSource` into each block's `ComponentPropsMap`)** is the wrong shape and the biggest change: the key is declared **once** on `PageComponentSchema` precisely because it applies to every page component, and copying it into 25+ per-block props schemas re-creates the hand-kept copies **as spec text**.
- **A** derives the accepted set from `PageComponentSchema`'s own key shape, moves with the spec, and still reds on an invented key.

⛔ **But this seat does not get to decide it there, and neither does a comment on this card.** A cross-seat request is work: it goes into the target lane's queue **as a card**, not as prose in an issue the other lane does not read. Filing it in `objectstack` with the implementer's measurement and calibration intact — the gate lives in `scripts/`, so grading and the `domain:*` label are that repo's triage's to produce, not mine.

⚠️ **Filing is blocked on a duplicate check, not on willingness.** The implementer could not file precisely because its dedup search returned `API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 319429713`, and it declined to file blind — the right call. My own dedup search just hit the same limit. ⇒ the card goes up as soon as a search returns, and this seat carries it until then rather than dropping it.

### Two things from this PR that the card did not anticipate, recorded here

⭐ **The population is 17 renderers in 13 files across 12 packages, not the card's nine** — and that is the injection form paying off exactly as ruled. Nothing was hand-listed, so the mechanism simply covered `plugin-grid`, `plugin-timeline`, two further `plugin-form` blocks and `element:record_picker` as well.

⭐ **`element:record_picker` was found by the render probe, not by reading sources.** It consumes the gate's **hook and status panels without the wrapper tag** ⇒ a tag-only check would have called it **compliant while it published this exact defect**. The new gate's rule was widened to the family the probe sees. An instrument that would have been wrong in a way that looks right is the most valuable thing this card produced.

### Recorded

- The new `check:element-data-source-declaration` gate fails any source that consumes the seam without reaching it — the mechanical half of *"a new block cannot forget"*, which is more than the ruling asked for and is what stops the tenth block from re-opening this card.
- `sdui-parser/src/validate.ts` and `BASE_PROPS` are **untouched** — I verified this from the diff's file list. Refused option A did not return through a side door.
- No block hand-writes the declaration: `name: 'dataSource'` appears **0** times in added lines across all `packages/plugin-*`. The plugin edits are one-line adoptions of `elementDataSourceBlock(...)`.
- ⭐ Process note worth keeping: the implementer **killed its own broad verification run mid-flight** because it was holding the shared verify lock while three sibling agents had been queued ~13 minutes, then re-ran a declared narrowing instead. Shared-resource discipline nobody asked it for.

⛔ No verdict on PR #6767 yet — its check table has not been read, and `in_progress` is not a pass.
